projects.name: Procurement of farm tools and implements procured (Procurement of farm tools and implements procured (line level, rope, range pole, Pick Axe, Crow bar, Sledge hammer)
projects.description: This includes the procurement of essential farm tools and implements such as line levels, ropes, range poles, pick axes, crow bars, and sledge hammers. Additionally, the purchase or production of organic fertilizer supports soil health. Key infrastructural projects like the construction of micro dams and the supply, installation, commissioning, and training of solar pumps are vital for efficient water management. The implementation of the Sememo and Merhano irrigation schemes, along with the installation of six additional drip irrigation sites, enhances irrigation capacity. A detailed study of six existing irrigation schemes will provide insights for future improvements. Moreover, the proper disposal of unwanted veterinary drugs and biologics, along with obsolete pesticides and their containers, is essential for environmental safety.
projects.outcome: Capacity of public sector is strengthened to develop strategies and policies for enterprise, job creation and employment.

projects.name: Develop Recipes and complementary foods from aquatic foods
projects.description:
Initiatives are being launched to develop recipes and complementary foods derived from aquatic sources, enhancing nutritional options for communities. A Social Behavior Communication Change (SBCC) strategy is being crafted to encourage increased fish consumption among households and communities. As part of this effort, procurement of aquatic food packaging and labeling materials is essential to promote these products effectively. Nutrition materials and equipment are also being acquired to support these initiatives, alongside a comprehensive fish consumption survey to gather valuable data.

In addition, new parameters are being introduced for research, including analyzing shelf life, assessing seaweed, and cultivating various purpose-driven microbes. To improve local fish distribution, procurement of eight ready-made retail fish shops and five solar-powered refrigerated fish transporting trucks is underway. The construction of ten solar-powered ice-producing facilities will further enhance fish preservation and quality.

Moreover, the procurement of 20 long line drum haulers and complete long line fishing gear for artisanal boats will support local fishermen. Plans include establishing fish drying facilities and renovating existing fish processing facilities to improve operational efficiency. Additional procurement of fishing inputs, the erection of ice plants, and the acquisition of water trucks are all part of a comprehensive approach to enhance the fishing industry. Finally, hatcheries are being established to support sustainable fish production and resource management.
projects.outcome: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability

projects.name: Equip Agri Statistics office at HQ and Zobas as well as front line extension officers with essential data collection  tools,
projects.description: Efforts are underway to equip the Agri Statistics office at headquarters and in Zobas, as well as frontline extension officers, with essential data collection tools. This initiative includes conducting surveys, data collection, and analysis, alongside carrying out an agricultural census to gather vital information. To strengthen human resources, staff upgrading opportunities for MSc and PhD programs, as well as short-term training abroad, are being implemented. Additionally, scientific visits to research stations are encouraged to foster knowledge exchange and collaboration development with regional laboratories and research institutions. The procurement of laboratory equipment, general materials, reagents, chemicals, facilities, and consumables is also prioritized to enhance research capabilities. Furthermore, the maintenance of the vaccine production laboratory and laboratory buildings, as well as the service and maintenance of laboratory equipment, are essential for ensuring operational efficiency. Finally, efforts are being made to rehabilitate the Ghinda regional laboratory, further supporting the advancement of agricultural research and statistics.
projects.outcome: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability

projects.name: Procurement of irrigation infrastructure maintenance supplies and field tools
projects.description: The procurement of irrigation infrastructure maintenance supplies and field tools is essential for ensuring the longevity and efficiency of agricultural operations. This includes the acquisition of spare parts and maintenance supplies, as well as the supply, installation, and commissioning of three automatic weather stations. Additionally, laboratory equipment and chemical reagents are being procured to support various agricultural functions. To ensure high standards, a seed quality control and certification system is being established, along with a national pest surveillance system. Technical assistance is also being provided to develop a registration system for animal drugs and biologics. Furthermore, office facilities are being procured for four existing and eight new animal quarantine stations, accompanied by necessary lab equipment and chemical reagents. Efforts are underway to develop an agro-mapping and agro-geospatial information system, as well as an agriculture market information system. Lastly, the procurement of equipment and materials aimed at expanding the agricultural innovation system will further enhance the sector's overall productivity and resilience.
projects.outcome: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability

projects.name: Introduction of Sexed bull semen and conduct mass insemination
projects.description:
The introduction of sexed bull semen is set to improve breeding efficiency, accompanied by mass insemination efforts to enhance livestock quality. Additionally, the purchase of backyard parent stock chicks will support local poultry production. To bolster veterinary services, equipment and materials are being procured for 73 veterinary clinics across six Zobas, ensuring that these facilities are well-equipped to serve livestock health needs.

Veterinary drugs and vaccines are also being purchased to maintain animal health and prevent disease outbreaks. For beekeepers in two Zobas, two honey processing plants will be acquired to enhance honey production and processing capabilities. Furthermore, procurement of ewes and rams will aid in the improvement of sheep breeding programs. Research will be conducted on breed selection, feeding practices, and health management to optimize livestock productivity.

Supplementary feed purchases are planned to ensure that animals receive adequate nutrition. Additionally, the procurement of Begait cattle and H. Friesian bulls will diversify and improve the genetic stock available to farmers, while the purchase of medicaments will support the overall health and productivity of livestock. These initiatives collectively aim to enhance the resilience and efficiency of the livestock sector.

projects.name: Maintenance of seed conditioning and processing plants
projects.description: Efforts are underway to maintain seed conditioning and processing plants, ensuring they operate at optimal efficiency. This includes the procurement of mobile seed conditioning and processing machines, as well as a chips-making machine. Additionally, small-scale fruit peeling, drying, and processing machines are being purchased to support local food production. The procurement of vitro plants will enhance the propagation of high-quality crops, while both expendable and non-expendable items are being acquired to support various agricultural functions. In vitro multiplication is being implemented for seed potatoes, bananas, sweet potatoes, date palms, and aloe vera, promoting diverse agricultural outputs. Furthermore, new materials for various staple crop seeds are being introduced, accompanied by experiments and trials to assess their viability. Foundation seed production is also a priority, along with ongoing trials on bio-pesticides and fungicides to explore sustainable pest management solutions.

framework.name: HUMAN DEVELOPMENT AND WELLBEING
framework.description:
The Human Development and Wellbeing priority 
area seeks to improve the prosperity and wellbeing 
of all Eritreans. It focuses on a wide range of areas, 
including health and nutrition, education, water, sanitation and hygiene, immunization, and energy. It also 
addresses issues around general governance, public 
management, and accountability. This priority has two 
outcomes that respond to at least nine (9) SDGs (on 
Health, Education, Water and Sanitation, Gender Equality, Affordable and Clean Energy, Reduced Inequality, 
Peace, and Strong Institution and Partnerships), along 
with national priorities

framework.name: INCLUSIVE, DIVERSIFIED AND CLIMATE RESILIENT ECONOMY
framework.description:
he Inclusive, Diversified and Climate-Resilient priority 
area acknowledges that climate change affects each 
aspect of sustainable development with profound 
and potentially lasting implications for people, planet, 
partnerships, and prosperity. The pursuit of an inclusive and diversified economy would have to be climate 
resilient to generate and sustain the gains required for 
achieving medium and long-term development goals. 
This priority area focuses on multi-dimensional poverty, 
hunger and food security, agriculture, livelihood, job opportunities and employment. It also focuses on climate 
change, sustainable natural resources management, 
disaster risk reduction and mitigation, biodiversity, 
responsible consumption and production, urbanization, 
sustainable cities and communities, conservation, and 
environmental degradation.
This priority area also focuses on about twelve (12) 
of the SDGs, namely Poverty, Hunger, Decent Work, 
Gender, Inequality, Industry, Innovation and infrastructure, Sustainable Cities and Communities, Responsible 
Consumption and Production and Climate Action, Life 
below Water, Life on Land, and the Partnership Goals
2. Secure sufficient, reliable and sustainable
production and supply of affordable energy
throughout Eritrea
3. Protection and rehabilitation of the environment
and enhancement of the ecosystem and life
supporting services
